title: Sampling variation and CI coverage
code_simulate:
set.seed(240506)
d <- data.frame(experiment=rep(1:1000, each=25),
                waiting_days=rexp(25000, rate=.2))
write.csv(d, file.path(out_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
plot(NA, xlim=range(c(low[1:60], high[1:60])), ylim=c(1,60),
     xlab="Mean waiting time and 95% t interval (days)", ylab="Simulated experiment")
abline(v=5, lty=2, lwd=2)
segments(low[1:60], 1:60, high[1:60], 1:60,
         col=ifelse(covered[1:60], "#146A85", "#C56B3B"), lwd=2)
points(estimate[1:60], 1:60, pch=16, cex=.5)
code_analysis:
low <- high <- estimate <- numeric(1000)
for (i in 1:1000) {
  x <- d$waiting_days[d$experiment==i]
  estimate[i] <- mean(x)
  margin <- qt(.975, length(x)-1)*sd(x)/sqrt(length(x))
  low[i] <- mean(x)-margin; high[i] <- mean(x)+margin
}
covered <- low<=5 & high>=5
result <- data.frame(experiment=1:1000, estimate, low, high, covered)
biology: Independent cell cultures differ in the waiting time to a developmental transition.
design: Repeat a 25-cell sampling experiment 1000 times from a known population.
question: How often does a stated interval procedure cover the true population mean?
null: This is a performance simulation, not a single hypothesis test. The known population mean is 5 days.
options: Choose sample size n independently of simulation count B.
Evaluate the same interval procedure in every experiment.
Check coverage against the fixed generating parameter.
assumptions: The simulated population reflects the scenario of interest.
Results describe this population, design and sample size.
parametric: Change n or the population distribution to examine the t interval.
nonparametric: Compare a bootstrap interval by repeating the entire sampling experiment.
generating_model: 1000 samples of 25 independent Exponential(rate=0.2/day) observations. Every sample uses a conventional two-sided 95% t interval for its mean.
generating_truth: The population mean is exactly 5 days; nominal 95% coverage is a procedure property to evaluate, not an imposed simulation result.
teaching_point: Larger B stabilizes the estimated coverage; larger n changes the experiment.

plot_args.note: Colors intervals by whether they contain the truth

practice: Would increasing the number of simulations give an individual experiment more biological replication?
